artworks.title: The Rape of Proserpina
artworks.description: A virtuoso Baroque marble group carved by the young Gian Lorenzo Bernini, showing Pluto — the Roman Hades — seizing Proserpina as she twists away from him. The god's fingers pressing into her marble flesh are celebrated as a technical marvel, and the three-headed Cerberus guards the base. The sculpture stands in the Galleria Borghese in Rome.

films.title: Hercules
films.description: Disney's Hades — blue flame, fast talk, soul contracts — stole the film and became the modern face of the underworld king for a generation.

music.title: Hadestown
music.description: Mitchell's folk-jazz musical rebuilds the underworld as an industrial company town: Hades the boss, Persephone his seasonal wife, Orpheus the boy who walks in singing — and walks out alone.

popCulture.title: Hades
popCulture.creator: Supergiant Games
popCulture.description: Supergiant's breakout names the game after him and then makes him a father: stern, wounded, and the boss at the end of every escape Zagreus attempts.

popCulture.title: Hades II
popCulture.creator: Supergiant Games
popCulture.description: The sequel keeps the house of Hades at its centre — now through Melinoë, the daughter raised to wage war while her father is held by Chronos.

popCulture.title: Kingdom Hearts
popCulture.creator: Square
popCulture.description: Disney's Hades crosses into Square's crossover RPG as a recurring schemer in Olympus Coliseum — the same blue flame, now trading blows with Sora.
